sentences.text:
This misc. appeal u/S. 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by appellant/claimant seeking enhancement of compensation amount by taking exception to the Award dated 06.10.2009 passed by 9th Additional Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (fast track), Gwalior (M.P.) (in short "Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No.106/2009, whereby the Claims Tribunal has awarded Rs.3,10,000/- along with interest from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization in favour of claimant on account of death of Hukum Singh in a motor accident.
2.The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are not in question.
3.

Challenging the impugned Award, it is contended on behalf of appellant that the Claims Tribunal has committed an error in awarding NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:391 2 MA-1502-2009 amount of compensation which is on lower side.
It is further submitted that at the time of accident, deceased was working as a puncture repair technician.
Therefore, his income must be assessed according to Minimum Wages Act but Claims Tribunal assessed income of deceased Rs.30,000/- per annum only.

It is further contended that the Claims Tribunal committed error in not awarding reasonable compensation under the head of loss of consortium, in not applying an appropriate multiplier, in failing to add the component of future prospects, and in not granting just and reasonable amounts under other conventional heads, such as loss of estate and funeral Smt.Anita vs Narendra Singh on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86468201/
1 expenses.
Hence, it is prayed that a reasonable and just amount of compensation be awarded to the claimant by enhancing the impugned Award.
Therefore, it is prayed that impugned award be set aside and just and reasonable amount of compensation be awarded to the claimant.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation and argued in support of the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal.
5. Having heard learned Counsel for the parties and perused the impugned award as well as record of Claims Tribunal 6.

In view of the judgments in Sukhdevi v. Devendra Kumar , ILR 2014 MP 172; Kanwar Devi v.
Bansal Roadways , 2008 ACJ 2182; and National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Renu Devi , (2008) 3 ACC 134 , when documentary proof of income is lacking, income is to be assessed as per the minimum wages applicable.

sentences.text:
It is found that Tribunal awarded compensation in favour NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:391 3 MA-1502-2009 of appellant only assessing income i.e. Rs.30,000/-
per annum which is not correct in the eye of law.
Compensation amount must be assessed only on the basis of Minimum Wages Act i.e. 3,195/- per month.

7. As regards loss of income including future prospects, in the light of judgment of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi , 2017 ACJ 2700 , the claimant is entitled for loss of income including future prospects of 40% and as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 , even if age of the deceased is to be taken into account, multiplier of 18 should be applied and 1/3 personal expenses of deceased should be deducted.

8. Accordingly, appellant-claimant is entitled to get compensation under the following heads:-
 HEAD AMOUNT  Income Rs.3195X 12= 38340  After adding Future Prospects@40% Rs.53,676/-
 After adding Dependency 2/3 Rs.35,784/-
 Loss of Income Rs.644112  Other Heads:-
 Loss of Consortium Rs.40,000 X 3= 1,2  Loss of Estate and funeral expenses Rs.30,000/-
Total Compensation = R 9.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case i s Rs.7,94,112/- as against the Award of the Claims Tribunal of Rs.3,10,000/-.

Accordingly, the appellant/claimant is entitled to an additional NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:391 4 MA-1502-2009 sum of Rs.4,84,112/- over and above the amount, which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.

In the result, this miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed, by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.4,84,112/-.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest as fixed by the learned Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
The enhanced amount shall be paid to the appellants within a period of three months from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this order.
The remaining conditions imposed by the learned Claims Tribunal shall remain unaltered.

11. If the enhanced amount of compensation is in excess to the valuation of appeal, the difference of the Court fee (if not already paid) shall be deposited by the appellant-claimant within a period of one month and proof thereof, shall be submitted before the Registry.
Thereafter, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of the order passed today.
12. In view of the above, miscellaneous appeal filed by the appellant/claimant stands disposed of.
